title: Reestablishing a start configuration
statement: Let $S$ be a setting, and suppose a start configuration for a statement $s$ at depth $d$, code position $\mathrm{pos}$, and stack position $q$ satisfies the start conditions. Let $t$ be a statement with compiled code at position $\mathrm{pos}'$, whose code length ends at or before the dispatcher, and whose width is at most $S.F$. Suppose $\sigma'$ is a state bounded by the limits of $S$, and a word-RAM memory $m'$ is related to $\sigma'$ at stack position $q$. Then $t$, $\sigma'$, $\mathrm{pos}'$, and $m'$ satisfy the start conditions for $S$ at depth $d$ and stack position $q$.
hypotheses_covered: An existing start configuration for $s$ at depth $d$, position $\mathrm{pos}$, and stack position $q$
The compiled code of $t$ occurs at $\mathrm{pos}'$
$m'$ is related to $\sigma'$ at stack position $q$
replaced:
Let $S$ be a setting, and suppose there is a start configuration for statement $s$ at
depth $d$, code position $\mathrm{pos}$, and stack position $q$. Suppose a statement $t$
has its compiled code at position $\mathrm{pos}'$, its code length ends at or before the
dispatcher, its width is at most $S.F$, and a state $\sigma'$ is bounded by
$S.\mathrm{lim}$. If a word-RAM memory $m'$ is related to $\sigma'$ at stack position
$q$, then $t$, $\sigma'$, $\mathrm{pos}'$, and $m'$ satisfy the start conditions for $S$
at the same depth $d$ and stack position $q$.
